verses.1: My eyes have seen all this; my ears have heard and considered it.
verses.2: What I know, you also know. I am no more ignorant than you are.
verses.3: But I will speak to the Almighty, and I will argue my case before God.
verses.4: You, however, are physicians of lies, all of you, healers of emptiness.
verses.5: If only silence would come upon you and wisdom to you!
verses.6: Listen now to my argument; give ear to the words of my mouth.
verses.7: Do you speak falsely about God, and with Him do you speak deceit?
verses.8: Do you turn your face away? Do you become His adversaries?
verses.9: Would it be good if He were to examine you? If He were to treat you like a mortal, would you be found innocent?
verses.10: He will surely rebuke you; if you hide your face, He will see it.
verses.11: Are not His terrors enough to strike you, and His fears to fall upon you?
verses.12: Your memories vanish like dust; your body is like clay.
verses.13: Be silent before me, and I will speak. Let what is on me pass away.
verses.14: Why should I take flesh in my teeth, and set my soul under my hand?
verses.15: Behold, if He should kill me, I will still trust in Him. I will argue my way before Him.
verses.16: For He is my salvation. No one who is wicked before Him can come to Him.
verses.17: Listen, hear my words. Let my message be heard by your ears.
verses.18: Look, I have arranged my case before you. I have known that I will be vindicated.
verses.19: Who is there who will contend with me? Let it be now, and I will fall silent.
verses.20: But only do not do two things to me. Then I will not hide from Your face.
verses.21: Turn Your hand away from me, and let Your fear not terrify me.
verses.22: Then call, and I will answer. Or speak, and I will respond.
verses.23: How many are my sins and my iniquities? Let me know my transgression and my sin.
verses.24: Why do You hide Your face, and count me as Your enemy?
verses.25: Do You lift up a wind to trouble me, and chase dry stubble with a storm?
verses.26: For You have written down bitter things against me, and recalled my childhood sins.
verses.27: You have set a snare for my feet, and watched all my paths, searching out every root of my steps.
verses.28: And I am like a potsherd that is broken, like a moth-eaten garment.

notes:
Notes
- v. 14: "set my soul under my hand" — reflects the Hebrew metaphor of self-preservation and resolve.
- v. 15: "I will still trust in Him" — the translation of "I will argue my way before Him" follows the context of Job's determination to present his case.
- v. 25: "dry stubble" — the Hebrew uses a metaphor that evokes something easily destroyed or consumed by wind.
